sources.scope: Official identity: full-time Psychology in Dutch and English.
Official course themes, three Year 3 specialisations, applied societal challenges and statement that students write a thesis.
Official 2026–27 overview. The current course repository link yielded a shell rather than course text.
2026–27 EER adopted 12 May 2026, 2024 curriculum. Articles 3.3 and 3.5–3.7, 5.2.2, 5.5 and Overview 2 control the workload, elective rules and progression.

Official 2025–26 English catalogue for the same 2024 curriculum in Years 1 and 2. Used to verify syllabus content including statistics, programming, psychometrics and the supervised group research project. The older Year 3 structure does not control the comparison.
Graduate examples and postgraduate routes, used as search context.

curriculum: The 2026–27 EER covers both language tracks of the 2024 curriculum. Overview 2 identifies three 60 EC study units. At 28 hours per credit, the first year has four 8 EC core modules, scientific inquiry blocks of 4, 4 and 8 EC, and 12 EC of professional skills. The two Scientific Inquiry II entries have distinct periods and workloads, 112 and 224 hours, so both appear once. Year 2 has a 16 EC Citizenship module, four 8 EC components and 12 EC skills. Year 3 has 24 EC electives, 24 EC specialisation and 12 EC skills. The first-listed Brain, Cognition and Behaviour option has four 168-hour modules. The two other tracks are alternatives, each of equal workload. These values describe workload within yearly credit awards. The programme page mentions a thesis. The EER does not identify its placement or allocate separate credit, so no extra component is added. The 8 EC-equivalent Year 2 Research Project is identified and the catalogue describes small groups supervised through the research cycle.
progression: Article 5.5 limits assessments by year. Article 5.2.2 awards a pass and 60 credits when all five competencies are at least on track, with conditional progression possible under the specified remediation rules. The usual route assumes a pass each year and follows Overview 2. Year 3 elective choices remain open within Article 3.7, with requirements for external or alternative packages. A portfolio records programme assessment in each year and does not create a second credit award. The 2026–27 Year 3 specialisation structure is verified through the regulations rather than relying on old third-year course descriptions.
